evidence: Ov. F. 1.149: quārē novus incipit annus
terms.comment: With an infinitive, with an object, or alone, and things begin too (incipit annus). For the past say coepī: Cicero uses incipiō only in the present system (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Hor. Ep. 1.2.40: dīmidium factī, quī coepit, habet
terms.comment: The past of “begin”; with a passive infinitive it is passive too: ars habērī coepta (Liv. 39.6.9).

evidence: Mart. 13.36.2: inchoat atque eadem fīnit olīva dapēs
terms.comment: Of starting something that is to be finished: a building, a book, a meal.

evidence: Cic. Phil. 14.36: facere initium cōnflīgendī (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 1.1.5: initium capit ā flūmine Rhodanō, of a region that begins at a river

phrases.latin: dīmidium factī, quī coepit, habet; sapere audē, incipe
phrases.english: well begun is half done: dare to be wise, and begin

phrases.latin: dīc, age, frīgoribus quārē novus incipit annus, quī melius per vēr incipiendus erat?
phrases.english: Come, tell me: why does the new year begin in the cold, when it would better have been begun in spring?

phrases.latin: animadvertuntque ea, quae domī fīunt, cūriōsius incipiuntque commentārī aliquid et discere
phrases.english: and they watch what goes on at home more keenly, and begin to make things up and to learn

phrases.latin: dum haec Taurus, intereā puer vēnerat et aula dēferbuerat tempusque esse coeperat edendī et tacendī
phrases.english: while Taurus was saying this, the boy had come in, the pot had stopped boiling, and it was time to eat and stop talking
